scenes.card: Built during the event. A research tool, not medical advice.
scenes.vo: Everything here was built during this event. It is a research tool, not medical advice. This is a pharmacogenomic lab report from India, travelling the way they really travel: a photograph on WhatsApp.

scenes.card: India's evidence base: two studies, about 3,600 people.
scenes.vo: India's evidence on these gene variants rests on two studies and about three and a half thousand people. Thousands of reports like this are issued every year. None of them reach a dataset.
Muse Spark reads the photograph under a strict schema, quoting every gene call from the page and recording which variants the laboratory says it tested.

scenes.card: PharmCAT standardises. Deterministic rules check coverage.
scenes.vo: PharmCAT, the engine behind the CPIC guidelines, standardises the allele names. Our rules check which India-relevant variants this panel never tested, and every identifier is stripped before storage.

scenes.card: The same photograph, on open weights.
scenes.vo: The same report, read again by Muse Spark Open. Open weights mean a biobank can run this inside its own network, the only version that could ever touch a real patient's report.

scenes.card: Muse Voice. Malayalam and English, mixed.
scenes.vo: Muse Voice takes results read aloud, Malayalam and English mixed the way people speak in a Kochi clinic. Muse Spark reads that transcript into the same record.

scenes.card: A human curator signs off every call.
scenes.vo: A curator checks each call against its quoted source. Muse Spark web search pulls what has been published for India, with sources.

scenes.card: Carrier frequencies. Wilson intervals. One CSV.
scenes.vo: Every reviewed record joins a cohort. Carrier frequencies with confidence intervals, honest denominators, and one download that is ready for a study.

We did not grade ourselves on our own fixtures. We ran it against two public sources of truth: the CDC's reference materials programme, and real 30x genomes from the Thousand Genomes Project. Two hundred and eight real people. Ninety-six percent of gene calls agree with the laboratory consensus, and every mismatch is traced.

scenes.card: The benchmark argued our own case.
scenes.vo: The benchmark also made our argument for us. Six disagreements were decreased-function alleles the consensus panel never looked for, all six African-ancestry samples: a panel designed elsewhere, calling a carrier a non-carrier.

Because reading the report is the easy half. We simulated a hundred and twenty Indian people, each with a report from a lab that tests only part of the panel. Counting an untested panel as a negative puts the carrier frequency at fifteen percent. The truth was twenty-five: a ten point error, downward, on the variant a quarter of Indians carry.
Pathya. Research data, from the reports India already has.
